title.zh: 卷十九 列傳第十三 宗夬 劉坦 樂藹
title.en: Volume 19: Zong Guai; Liu Tan; Yue Ai
title.raw: 卷十九 列傳第十三 宗夬 劉坦 樂藹 Volume 19: Zong Guai; Liu Tan; Yue Ai

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第十九 列傳第十三

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 19, Biographies 13
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 19, Biographies 13

sentences.zh: 宗夬 劉坦 樂藹

translations.literal: Zong Guai; Liu Tan; Yue Ai
translations.idiomatic: Zong Guai; Liu Tan; Yue Ai

sentences.zh: 宗夬字明敭，南陽涅陽人也，世居江陵。

translations.literal: Zong Guai, styled Mingyang, was a native of Nieyang in Nanyang; his family had long dwelt in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Guai, styled Mingyang, came from Nieyang in Nanyang; his line had long lived in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 祖炳，宋時徵太子庶子不就，有高名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bing, in Song times summoned as crown prince attendant but did not accept, had a lofty name.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bing, summoned in Song as crown prince attendant but never took the post, was widely esteemed.

sentences.zh: 父繁，西中郎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Fan was a staff adviser to the western army commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan served as staff adviser to the western army commander.

sentences.zh: 夬少勤學，有局幹。

translations.literal: Guai from youth studied hard and had breadth and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Guai studied hard and showed both breadth and backbone.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，舉郢州秀才，歷臨川王常侍、驃騎行參軍。

translations.literal: At his capping he was recommended as Yingzhou's outstanding talent and served as attendant to the Prince of Linchuan, then as staff officer on the chief of staff's staff.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he was named Yingzhou's outstanding talent, then served the Prince of Linchuan and the chief of staff's staff.

sentences.zh: 齊司徒竟陵王集學士于西邸，並見圖畫，夬亦預焉。

translations.literal: In Yongming, the Prince of Jingling of Qi gathered scholars at the Western Lodge and had them painted; Guai was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming the Prince of Jingling gathered scholars at the Western Lodge and had them painted; Guai was there.

sentences.zh: 永明中，與魏和親，敕夬與尚書殿中郎任昉同接魏使，皆時選也。

translations.literal: In Yongming, when peace was made with Wei, an edict had Guai and Palace Director Ren Fang receive the Wei envoys together—both were men of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi made peace with Wei in Yongming, Guai and Palace Director Ren Fang were chosen to receive the Wei envoys—both were men of the hour.

sentences.zh: 武帝嫡孫南郡王居西州，以夬管書記，夬旣以筆札被知，亦以貞正見許，故任焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor's eldest grandson, Prince of Nan commandery, dwelt at the Western Lodge; Guai was put in charge of his secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's eldest grandson, Prince of Nan commandery, held the Western Lodge; Guai ran his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄而文惠太子薨，王爲皇太孫，夬仍管書記。

translations.literal: Because his brushwork won notice and his uprightness won trust, he was entrusted with the post.
translations.idiomatic: His writing won notice and his rectitude trust, so he kept the post.

sentences.zh: 及太孫卽位，多失德，夬頗自疏，得爲秣陵令，遷尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: Before long Crown Prince Wenhuai died; the prince became heir apparent; Guai still managed the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Crown Prince Wenhuai died and the prince became heir apparent; Guai still kept the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隆昌末，少帝見誅，寵舊多罹其禍，惟夬及傅昭以清正免。

translations.literal: When the heir took the throne he lost his way in many things; Guai drew somewhat apart, was made Moling magistrate, and was promoted to Director of Punishments in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir took the throne his conduct slipped; Guai kept his distance, became Moling magistrate, then Director of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 夬從弟岳，有名行，州裏稱之，出於夬右。

translations.literal: Guai's cousin Yue had a famed conduct; the district praised him and ranked him above Guai.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yue was famed for conduct; the district praised him above Guai.

sentences.zh: 仕歷尚書庫部郎，郢州治中，北中郎錄事參軍事。

translations.literal: In office he rose through Director of the Arsenal in the Masters of Writing, Yingzhou chief clerk, and recorder on the northern army commander's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Director of the Arsenal, Yingzhou chief clerk, and recorder on the northern army staff.

sentences.zh: 劉坦，字德度，南陽安衆人也，晉鎮東將軍喬之七世孫。

translations.literal: Liu Tan, styled Dedu, was a native of Anzhong in Nanyang, seventh-generation descendant of Jin's general who guarded the east, Liu Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan, styled Dedu, came from Anzhong in Nanyang, seventh in descent from Jin's eastern guardian Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 坦少爲從兄虯所知。

translations.literal: From youth Tan was known to his elder cousin Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: From youth his elder cousin Jiao knew him.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，爲南郡王國常侍，尋補孱陵令，遷南中郎錄事參軍，所居以幹濟稱。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan in Qi he was attendant to the Prince of Nan commandery; soon he supplemented as magistrate of Chanling, was promoted to recorder on the southern army staff, and where he served was praised for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi's Jianyuan opening he attended the Prince of Nan commandery, soon became Chanling magistrate, then southern army recorder, famed everywhere for capable rule.

sentences.zh: 南康王爲荊州刺史，坦爲西中郎中兵參軍，領長流。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nankang was inspector of Jingzhou, Tan was middle army staff officer on the western staff, leading the long current.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nankang held Jingzhou, Tan was western staff middle army officer, leading the long current.

sentences.zh: 義師起，遷諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the Righteous Army rose, he was promoted staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous Army rose, he became staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 時輔國將軍楊公則爲湘州刺史，帥師赴夏口，西朝議行州事者，坦謂衆曰：「湘境人情，易擾難信。

translations.literal: At the time supporting-the-state general Yang Gongze was inspector of Xiangzhou and led troops to Xia mouth; the western court debated who should act as inspector; Tan told the assembly: "The temper of Xiang country is easy to stir and hard to trust.
translations.idiomatic: Supporting-the-state general Yang Gongze was Xiangzhou inspector, marching to Xia mouth; the western court debated who should run the province; Tan said, "Xiang country is quick to stir and slow to trust.

sentences.zh: 若專用武士，則百姓畏侵漁；

translations.literal: If you rely on warriors alone, the people will fear plunder;
translations.idiomatic: Send only warriors and the people fear plunder;

sentences.zh: 若遣文人，則威略不振。

translations.literal: if you send men of letters alone, authority and strategy will not hold.
translations.idiomatic: send only men of letters and authority will not hold.

sentences.zh: 必欲鎮靜一州城，軍民足食，則無逾老臣。

translations.literal: If you truly wish to quiet a whole province, feed army and people alike, none surpasses this old servant.
translations.idiomatic: To quiet the province and feed army and people, none surpasses this old servant.

sentences.zh: 先零之役，竊以自許。

translations.literal: In the campaign against the Xianlian—I dare claim that for myself."
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianlian campaign—I dare answer for that."

sentences.zh: 」遂從之。

translations.literal: They followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: They took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 乃除輔國長史、長沙太守，行湘州事。

translations.literal: He was made chief of staff to the supporting-the-state army, grand administrator of Changsha, and acting inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supporting-the-state chief of staff, Changsha grand administrator, and acting Xiangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 坦嘗在湘州，多舊恩，道迎者甚衆。

translations.literal: Tan had once served in Xiangzhou and had many old ties; a great crowd came to meet him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He had served in Xiang before and held many ties; crowds met him on the road.

sentences.zh: 下車簡選堪事吏，分詣十郡，悉發人丁，運租米三十餘萬斛，致之義師，資糧用給。

translations.literal: On taking office he chose able clerks and sent them to the ten commanderies, mustered laborers everywhere, and moved more than three hundred thousand hu of tax grain to the Righteous Army so supplies held.
translations.idiomatic: He chose able clerks for ten commanderies, mustered labor, and forwarded three hundred thousand hu of tax grain to the Righteous Army.

sentences.zh: 時東昏遣安成太守劉希祖破西臺所選太守范僧簡於平都，希祖移檄湘部，於是始興內史王僧粲應之。

translations.literal: At the time Donghun sent Ancheng grand administrator Liu Xizu to defeat the western court's chosen grand administrator Fan Senjian at Pingdu; Xizu issued a proclamation across Xiang, and then Shixing interior governor Wang Sengru answered him.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun's Liu Xizu defeated the western court's Fan Senjian at Pingdu and issued a call across Xiang; Shixing interior governor Wang Sengru answered.

sentences.zh: 邵陵人逐其內史褚洊，永陽人周暉起兵攻始安郡，並應僧粲。

translations.literal: Shaoling men drove out their interior governor Chu Zhan; Yongyang men Zhou Hui raised troops and attacked Shian commandery—all answered Sengru.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoling drove out Chu Zhan; Yongyang's Zhou Hui attacked Shian—all joined Sengru.

sentences.zh: 桂陽人邵曇弄、鄧道介報復私仇，因合黨亦同焉。

translations.literal: Guiyang men Shao Tanlong and Deng Daojie, settling private scores, also joined the league.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang's Shao Tanlong and Deng Daojie, settling private scores, joined as well.

sentences.zh: 僧粲自號平西將軍、湘州刺史，以永陽人周舒爲謀主，師于建寧。

translations.literal: Sengru styled himself pacifying-the-west general and inspector of Xiangzhou, made Yongyang man Zhou Shu his strategist, and camped at Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru called himself pacifying-the-west general and Xiangzhou inspector, set Zhou Shu of Yongyang as strategist, and camped at Jianning.

sentences.zh: 自是湘部諸郡，悉皆蜂起；

translations.literal: From then on commanderies across Xiang rose like hornets;
translations.idiomatic: Then every Xiang commandery rose;

sentences.zh: 惟臨湘、湘陰、瀏陽、羅四縣猶全。

translations.literal: only Linxiang, Xiangyin, Liuyang, and Luo four counties still held whole.
translations.idiomatic: only Linxiang, Xiangyin, Liuyang, and Luo still stood intact.

sentences.zh: 州人咸欲泛舟逃走，坦悉聚船焚之，遣將尹法略距僧粲，相持未決。

translations.literal: The people of the province all wished to flee by boat; Tan gathered every vessel and burned them, sent the general Yin Falüe to hold off Sengru, and the two sides locked in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: The province meant to flee by boat; Tan burned the fleet, sent Yin Falüe against Sengru, and stalemate followed.

sentences.zh: 前湘州鎮軍鐘玄紹潛謀應僧粲，要結士庶數百人，皆連名定計，刻日反州城。

translations.literal: Former Xiangzhou garrison commander Zhong Xuanshao secretly plotted to join Sengru, mustering several hundred gentry and commoners by linked names to a fixed day for a rising in the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Former garrison commander Zhong Xuanshao plotted for Sengru, binding hundreds of gentry to rise on a set day.

sentences.zh: 坦聞其謀，偽爲不知，因理訟至夜，而城門遂不閉，以疑之。

translations.literal: Tan heard the plot but feigned ignorance, heard lawsuits into the night, and left the gates unclosed to sow doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Tan heard but played ignorant, heard suits till night, and left the gates open to breed doubt.

sentences.zh: 玄紹未及發，明旦詣坦問其故。

translations.literal: Xuanshao had not yet moved; at dawn he came to Tan to ask why.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xuanshao moved, at dawn he came to ask why.

sentences.zh: 坦久留與語，密遣親兵收其家書。

translations.literal: Tan kept him long in talk and secretly sent trusted soldiers to seize his household papers.
translations.idiomatic: Tan detained him in talk and sent soldiers to seize his papers.

sentences.zh: 玄紹在坐未起，而收兵已報具得其文書本末，玄紹卽首伏，於坐斬之。

translations.literal: Xuanshao had not yet risen from his seat when the soldiers reported they had the documents entire; Xuanshao confessed at once and was beheaded where he sat.
translations.idiomatic: Still seated, Xuanshao learned the papers were taken; he confessed and was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 焚其文書，其餘黨悉無所問，衆愧且服，州部遂安。

translations.literal: The papers were burned; the rest of the party were not questioned; the crowd felt shame and yielded, and the province was quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The papers burned; the rest went untouched; shame and submission followed, and the province calmed.

sentences.zh: 法略與僧粲相持累月，建康城平，公則還州，羣賊始散。

translations.literal: Falüe and Sengru locked horns for months; when Jiankang fell, Gongze returned to the province and the rebels at last scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Falüe and Sengru fought for months; Jiankang fell, Gongze returned, and the rebels scattered.

sentences.zh: 天監初，論功封荔浦縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian, for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Lipu with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianjian's opening he was baron of Lipu with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷平西司馬、新興太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to western army marshal and grand administrator of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: He became western army marshal and Xinxing grand administrator.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，遷西中郎長史，卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In Tianjian year three he was promoted western army chief of staff and died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year three he was western army chief of staff and died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 子泉嗣。

translations.literal: His son Quan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 樂藹字蔚遠，南陽淯陽人，晉尚書令廣之六世孫，世居江陵。

translations.literal: Yue Ai, styled Weiyuan, was a native of Yuyang in Nanyang, sixth-generation descendant of Jin's Director of the Masters of Writing Guang, his family long in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ai, styled Weiyuan, came from Yuyang in Nanyang, sixth from Jin's Director Guang; his line lived in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 其舅雍州刺史宗愨，嘗陳器物，試諸甥侄。

translations.literal: His uncle, Jingzhou inspector Zong Que, once set out vessels and tested his nephews.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zong Que, Jingzhou inspector, once set out vessels to test his nephews.

sentences.zh: 藹時尚幼，而所取惟書，愨由此奇之。

translations.literal: Ai was still young but took only books; Que marveled at that.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was young but chose only books; Que marveled.

sentences.zh: 又取史傳各一卷授藹等，使讀畢，言所記。

translations.literal: He also gave each a scroll of histories and had them read and recite what they remembered.
translations.idiomatic: He gave each a history scroll, had them read, then recite from memory.

sentences.zh: 藹略讀具舉，愨益善之。

translations.literal: Ai skimmed and named every point; Que prized him still more.
translations.idiomatic: Ai skimmed and named every point; Que prized him more.

sentences.zh: 宋建平王景素爲荊州刺史，辟爲主簿。

translations.literal: Song's Prince of Pingyang Jingsu was inspector of Jingzhou and summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Prince of Pingyang, inspector of Jingzhou, made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 景素爲南徐州，復爲征北刑獄參軍，遷龍陽相。

translations.literal: When Jingsu held southern Xuzhou, Ai again served as staff officer on the northern punitive staff, then was promoted magistrate of Longyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsu held southern Xuzhou, Ai served on the northern punitive staff, then became Longyang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，吏民詣州請之，葬訖起焉。

translations.literal: He left office for his father's mourning; officials and people went to the province to ask him back, and after the burial he took up the post again.
translations.idiomatic: His father's mourning took him away; officials and people begged the province to recall him, and after burial he returned.

sentences.zh: 時齊豫章王嶷爲武陵太守，雅善藹爲政，及嶷爲荊州刺史，以藹爲驃騎行參軍、領州主簿，參知州事。

translations.literal: At the time Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Diao was grand administrator of Wuling and greatly prized Ai's governance; when Diao became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai staff officer on the chief of staff's staff and head clerk of the province, sharing in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Diao, Wuling grand administrator, prized his rule; as Jingzhou inspector Diao made Ai chief-of-staff staff officer and head clerk, sharing provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 嶷嘗問藹風土舊俗，城隍基啉寺，山川險易，藹隨問立對，若按圖牒，嶷益重焉。

translations.literal: Diao once asked him about local custom, old ways, city walls and foundations, temples, and mountain passes—Ai answered each question on the spot as if reading from a gazetteer, and Diao esteemed him the more.
translations.idiomatic: Diao asked about custom, walls, temples, and passes; Ai answered as from a map, and Diao esteemed him more.

sentences.zh: 州人嫉之，或譖藹廨門如市，嶷遣覘之，方見藹閉閣讀書。

translations.literal: Provincial men envied him; some slandered him, saying his office gate was like a market; Diao sent men to watch and found Ai behind closed doors reading.
translations.idiomatic: Envious men said his gate was a market; Diao watched and found him reading behind closed doors.

sentences.zh: 嶷還都，以藹爲太尉刑獄參軍，典書記，遷枝江令。

translations.literal: When Diao returned to the capital, Ai was made staff officer on the Grand Marshal's punitive staff, in charge of the secretariat, then magistrate of Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Diao returned to court; Ai became Grand Marshal punitive staff officer, ran the secretariat, then Zhijiang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 還爲大司馬中兵參軍，轉署記室。

translations.literal: On return he was middle army staff officer to the Grand Marshal, then acting recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Grand Marshal middle army officer, then acting recorder.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，荊州刺史巴東王子響稱兵反，旣敗，焚燒府舍，官曹文書，一時蕩盡。

translations.literal: In Yongming year eight the Prince of Badong Zixiang raised troops in rebellion; when he was defeated he burned the government offices and every document in the bureaus was lost at once.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year eight Prince Zixiang of Badong rebelled; defeated, he burned the offices and every record was lost.

sentences.zh: 武帝引見藹，問以西事，藹上對詳敏，帝悅焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Ai and asked about western affairs; Ai answered in full detail and the Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him, asked about the west; his answers pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 用爲荊州治中，敕付以修復府州事。

translations.literal: He was made Jingzhou chief clerk with orders to restore the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Jingzhou chief clerk and ordered to rebuild the seat.

sentences.zh: 藹還州，繕脩廨署數百區，頃之咸畢，而役不及民。

translations.literal: Ai returned to the province, repaired several hundred office compounds, and soon all were done while the labor did not burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the province he rebuilt hundreds of offices at once without burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 荊部以爲自晉王悅移鎮以來，府舍未之有也。

translations.literal: Jing region said that since Jin's Wang Yue moved his seat, no government house had matched it.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said that since Jin's Wang Yue moved the seat, no seat had matched it.

sentences.zh: 九年，豫章王嶷薨，藹解官赴喪，率荊、湘二州故吏，建碑墓所。

translations.literal: In year nine the Prince of Yuzhang Diao died; Ai left office to mourn, led former clerks of Jing and Xiang, and set a stele at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine Prince Diao died; Ai mourned, led old Jing and Xiang clerks, and raised a tomb stele.

sentences.zh: 累遷車騎平西錄事參軍、步兵校尉，求助戍西歸。

translations.literal: Through offices he rose to recorder on the chariot-and-cavalry pacifying-the-west staff and infantry commandant, and begged leave to guard the west on his return.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chariot-and-cavalry western recorder and infantry commandant, then begged leave to guard the west.

sentences.zh: 南康王爲西中郎，以藹爲諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nankang was western army commander, Ai was his staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nankang commanded the western army, Ai was staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 義師起，蕭穎胄引藹及宗夬、劉坦，任以經略。

translations.literal: When the Righteous Army rose, Xiao Yingzhou brought in Ai with Zong Guai and Liu Tan and entrusted them with strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous Army rose, Xiao Yingzhou brought in Ai, Zong Guai, and Liu Tan for strategy.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，遷鎮軍司馬、中書侍郎、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the Liang headquarters was founded, he was promoted to marshal of the army that guards the state, palace gentleman of the Secretariat, and Left Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang headquarters was founded, he became guarding-the-state marshal, Secretariat gentleman, and Left Director.

sentences.zh: 時營造器甲，舟艦軍糧，及朝廷儀憲，悉資藹焉。

translations.literal: At the time forging arms and armor, warships and army grain, and court ritual all drew on Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Forging arms, building ships, army grain, and court ritual all ran through Ai.

sentences.zh: 尋遷給事黃門侍郎，左丞如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate who attends to matters, Left Director as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Left Director unchanged.

sentences.zh: 和帝東下，道兼衛尉卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor He went east, Ai held the post of Commandant of the Guard on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He went east, Ai served as Commandant of the Guard on the road.

sentences.zh: 天監初，遷驍騎將軍、領少府卿；

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was promoted to Raiding Cavalry General and Director of the Palace Workshop;
translations.idiomatic: At Tianjian's opening he was Raiding Cavalry General and palace workshop director;

sentences.zh: 俄遷御史中丞，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: soon he was Censor-in-Chief and head of the great rectifiers of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: soon Censor-in-Chief and head of his province's great rectifiers.

sentences.zh: 初，藹發江陵，無故於船得八車輻，如中丞健步避道者，至是果遷焉。

translations.literal: When Ai had set out from Jiangling he found for no reason on the boat eight carriage hubs, like a censor's brisk step giving way on the road—and now the omen came true.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Jiangling he had found eight carriage hubs on the boat, like a censor stepping aside—and now the omen held.

sentences.zh: 藹性公強，居憲臺甚稱職。

translations.literal: Ai's nature was fair and forceful; at the censorate he filled the post admirably.
translations.idiomatic: Fair and forceful, he shone at the censorate.

sentences.zh: 時長沙宣武王將葬，而車府忽於庫火油絡，欲推主者。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Changsha, King Xuan of Wu, was to be buried, and the carriage office suddenly found lamp oil ablaze in the storehouse; they wished to impeach the keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuan of Changsha was to be buried when the carriage office found lamp oil burning in the storehouse and sought a culprit.

sentences.zh: 藹曰：「昔晉武庫火，張華以爲積油萬石必然。

translations.literal: Ai said: "In Jin, when the arsenal caught fire, Zhang Hua held that ten thousand stone of oil piled up made it inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Ai said, "When Jin's arsenal burned, Zhang Hua said ten thousand stone of piled oil made fire inevitable.

sentences.zh: 今庫若有灰，非吏罪也。

translations.literal: If the storehouse now holds ash, it is no clerk's crime."
translations.idiomatic: If ash lies in the storehouse, no clerk is to blame."

sentences.zh: 」旣而檢之，果有積灰。

translations.literal: On inspection there was indeed piled ash.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection found piled ash.

sentences.zh: 時稱其博物弘恕焉。

translations.literal: The age praised his broad learning and large forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The age praised his learning and his large forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 二年，出爲持節、督廣交越三州諸軍、冠軍將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In year two he went out bearer of staff, commander of military affairs in Guang, Jiao, and Yue, Champion General, pacifying-the-Yue middle army commander, and inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he went out with staff, commanding Guang, Jiao, and Yue, champion general, pacifying-the-Yue commander, and Guangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 前刺史徐元瑜罷歸，道遇始興人士反，逐內史崔睦舒，因掠元瑜財產。

translations.literal: The former inspector Xu Yuanyu left his post and on the road met Shixing men in revolt; they drove out interior governor Cui Mushu and plundered Yuanyu's goods.
translations.idiomatic: Former inspector Xu Yuanyu met Shixing rebels on the road; they drove out Cui Mushu and looted his goods.

sentences.zh: 元瑜走歸廣州，借兵於藹，托欲討賊，而實謀襲藹。

translations.literal: Yuanyu fled back to Guangzhou, borrowed troops from Ai on the pretext of punishing bandits, but in truth meant to strike Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu fled to Guangzhou, borrowed troops to hunt bandits, but meant to strike Ai.

sentences.zh: 藹覺之，誅元瑜。

translations.literal: Ai saw through it and executed Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ai saw through it and killed Yuanyu.

sentences.zh: 尋進號征虜將軍，卒官。

translations.literal: Soon his title advanced to general who campaigns against barbarians; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was general who campaigns against barbarians and died in office.

sentences.zh: 藹姊適徵士同郡劉虯，亦明識有禮訓。

translations.literal: Ai's elder sister married the reclusive Liu Jiao of the same commandery, also famed for discernment and ritual teaching.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister married the recluse Liu Jiao of his commandery, famed for discernment and ritual.

sentences.zh: 藹爲州，迎姊居官舍，參分祿秩，西土稱之。

translations.literal: When Ai was in the province he welcomed his sister to the official residence and shared his salary; the west praised it.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector he brought his sister to the yamen and shared salary; the west praised it.

sentences.zh: 子法才，字元備，幼與弟法藏俱有美名。

translations.literal: His son Facai, styled Yuanbei, in youth with his younger brother Fazang both had a fine name.
translations.idiomatic: His son Facai, styled Yuanbei, and his brother Fazang were both famed in youth.

sentences.zh: 少游京師，造沈約，約見而稱之。

translations.literal: Young, he traveled to the capital and visited Shen Yue; Yue saw him and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he visited Shen Yue at the capital; Yue praised him.

sentences.zh: 齊和帝爲相國，召爲府參軍，鎮軍蕭穎胄辟主簿。

translations.literal: When Qi's Emperor He was prime minister, Facai was summoned as staff officer to the prime minister's office; the army that guards the state, Xiao Yingzhou, made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He of Qi was prime minister, Facai joined his staff; Xiao Yingzhou made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，除起部郎。

translations.literal: When the Liang headquarters was founded, he was made Gentleman who initiates affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang headquarters was founded, he was Gentleman who initiates affairs.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，藹出鎮嶺表，法才留任京邑，遷金部郎，父憂去官。

translations.literal: In Tianjian year two, when Ai went out to command the southern frontier, Facai stayed in the capital, was promoted to Director of the Treasury, and left office for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year two Ai went south; Facai stayed at court as Director of the Treasury, then mourned his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除中書通事舍人，出爲本州別駕。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made Secretariat attendant who handles affairs and went out as chief clerk of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he handled Secretariat affairs and went out as native province chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 入爲通直散騎侍郎，復掌通事，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He entered as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, again handled affairs, and was promoted Right Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Regular Attendant, again handled affairs, then became Right Director.

sentences.zh: 晉安王爲荊州，重除別駕從事史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an held Jingzhou, he was again made chief clerk and staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin'an held Jingzhou, he was again chief clerk and staff officer.

sentences.zh: 復徵爲尚書右丞，出爲招遠將軍、建康令。

translations.literal: He was summoned again as Right Director, went out as general who invites from afar and magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Right Director, he went out as general who invites from afar and Jiankang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 不受俸秩，比去任，將至百金，縣曹啟輸臺庫。

translations.literal: He would not take salary; by the time he left office he had nearly a hundred jin of gold, and the county clerks reported it to the central treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He took no salary; near a hundred jin of gold had gathered when he left, and the county reported it to the central treasury.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其清節，曰：「居職若斯，可以爲百城表矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu prized his integrity and said: "To hold office like this is to stand as a model for a hundred cities.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu prized his integrity and said, "To hold office like this is to be a model for a hundred cities.

sentences.zh: 」卽日遷太府卿。

translations.literal: ” That same day he was transferred to Grand Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: ” That same day he was made grand chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 尋除南康內史，恥以讓俸受名，辭不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed interior administrator of Nankang; ashamed to accept the name of one who yielded his salary, he declined and did not take the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon named Nankang interior administrator, he refused the post rather than accept a title earned by yielding his salary.

sentences.zh: 俄轉雲騎將軍、少府卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Cloud-Cavalry General and Minister of Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became cloud-cavalry general and minister of palace supplies.

sentences.zh: 出爲信武長史、江夏太守。

translations.literal: He went out as chief clerk on the Trustworthy Martial staff and Jiangxia administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Trustworthy Martial chief clerk and Jiangxia administrator.

sentences.zh: 因被代，表便道還鄉。

translations.literal: When he was replaced, he memorialized to return home by the direct route.
translations.idiomatic: Replaced in office, he asked leave to go home by the direct route.

sentences.zh: 至家，割宅爲寺，棲心物表。

translations.literal: At home he divided his residence to make a temple and lodged his heart beyond worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At home he gave part of his house for a temple and turned his mind from the world.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以法才舊臣，累有優令，召使東下，未及發而卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: The crown prince, since Facai was an old retainer, repeatedly sent favorable orders summoning him east; before he could set out he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, holding Facai an old servant, sent him generous summons east again and again; he died before he could leave, at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：蕭穎胄起大州之衆以會義，當其時，人心未之能悟。

translations.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: Xiao Yingzhou raised the hosts of a great province to join the righteous cause; at that time men’s hearts had not yet understood.
translations.idiomatic: Chen minister of personnel Yao Cha said: Xiao Yingzhou gathered a great province’s forces for the founding cause; then few yet saw what was coming.

sentences.zh: 此三人者，楚之鎮也。

translations.literal: These three were Chu’s anchor.
translations.idiomatic: These three were Chu’s pillars.

sentences.zh: 經營締構，蓋有力焉。

translations.literal: In planning and building the foundation they surely had force.
translations.idiomatic: In planning and laying the foundations they surely did heavy work.

sentences.zh: 方面之功，坦爲多矣；

translations.literal: In regional achievements Tan had the greater share;
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier Tan did the heavier part;

sentences.zh: 當官任事，藹則兼之。

translations.literal: in holding office and managing affairs Ai had both.
translations.idiomatic: in office and in duty Ai had both.

sentences.zh: 咸登寵秩，宜乎！

translations.literal: All ascended to favored rank—fitting!
translations.idiomatic: All rose to favored rank—as they should!
